## Cherenkov light {#cherenkov-light}

### Why a cone?

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Light gets ahead** — $v<c/n$
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**The particle gets ahead** — $v>c/n$
:::
:::::

<img class="slide-media media-height-md" style="--media-max-height: 440px;" src="media/principles/cherenkov-slow-fast.svg" alt="Same-age wavefronts: below threshold the circles are nested; above threshold they share a tangent front behind the particle.">

::: {.takeaway}
The charge disturbs the medium. A fast charge leaves a common wavefront behind.
:::

### Which way does light go?

<img class="slide-media media-height-md" style="--media-max-height: 440px;" src="media/principles/cherenkov-light-direction.svg" alt="Light travels along a radius of a spherical wavefront, perpendicular to the common tangent front. The emission angle is measured from the forward particle track.">

**Light goes across the front — not along it.**

$$
\cos\theta_C=\frac{c}{nv}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\theta_C\simeq41^\circ\ \text{in water, for }v\simeq c.
$$

::::::

::: {.notes}
Use the new 40-second English film from
dvnanima/cherenkov_radiation/cherenkov_radiation.py. The former movie with
the angle graph and detector ring has been retired.

Four steps:
0–10 s: beta=0.55 below threshold, four wavefronts stay nested.
10–20 s: reset to a separate constant-speed beta=0.99 trial. Same phase index
and wavelet ages; the faster charge sits outside its earlier fronts.
20–28 s: freeze the charge AND wavefronts at the same physical clock value.
Reveal the white tangent front and the four contact points on each side.
28–40 s: show a ray from an earlier position, normal to the front. Highlight
the right angle; then show a second ray on the other side of the cone section.

The charge disturbs the medium. Circles represent a Huygens construction of
wavefronts, not four physically emitted photons or four optical emission
periods. Below threshold the drawing does not imply Cherenkov radiation.
Do not explain the effect as circles crossing: intersections are not the
criterion. The common front is tangent to all four circles. In three
dimensions it is a cone; the blue ray direction is perpendicular to its
surface, not along the white boundary.

The model uses c=1 in illustrative length/time units, a constant phase
index n=1.33, and wavelet creation times 0/0.5/1/1.5. The final physical
time is 2.6 in those units. Film time is slowed and paused for teaching.
All physical/style/movie values are in config.toml and all text/math labels
in texts.toml. No continuous acceleration is simulated: the fade at
10 seconds explicitly separates two uniform-motion examples. At fast
beta=0.99, theta_C=40.5821 degrees, rounded to about 41 degrees on screen.

The static comparison uses the same wavelet ages and speeds. The static
angle diagram uses the beta=1 limit (41.2465 degrees). Both are geometrical
illustrations. Tests check radius growth, nesting, charge outside the fast
fronts, tangencies, normal rays, frozen pauses and both-language label layout.

The phase-velocity threshold and angle are
$v>c/n$ and $\cos\theta_C=1/(n\beta)$. No photon yield, interference amplitudes,
wavelength dependence, absorption, scattering or detector response is
computed. Real photon travel times require a group index distinct from the
phase index; connect that distinction to slide 12 if asked.

The detailed kinetic thresholds and the old ring construction are optional
background, not visible-slide material: for n=1.33 the electron kinetic
threshold is 0.264 MeV and the muon threshold is 54.6 MeV. The ideal ring in
the old movie was a point-emission cone cut by a perpendicular screen, not
a neutrino-telescope hit pattern. Source/provenance:
media/principles/SOURCES.md and dvnanima/cherenkov_radiation/README.md.
:::
